editorial.question: Which important RAN1 and RAN4 choices are advancing, and what dependencies remain?
editorial.answer: Control signaling and mobility capability reuse advance, while beamforming cost, learned channel models, satellite access and sensing still depend on explicit implementation assumptions.
editorial.mechanism: An uplink grant can influence which logical channels are served through logical-channel prioritization.; Digital and analog spatial filtering move conversion and distribution costs between blocks.; Cross-site prediction depends on channel correlation that simple visibility labels do not supply.; Per-cell limits apply individually while across-cell resources cover the total candidate set.; Synchronization visibility and usable random-access occasions must follow beam activation.; Multiple views, detector processing and self-interference shape the result beyond echo signal quality.
editorial.tradeoff: Useful service differentiation versus control-message size and common access burden.; More digital chains versus removal of analog distribution and beamforming components.; Reproducible evaluation versus realistic deployment variation and model complexity.; Reuse of existing capabilities versus correct accounting across multiple configurations.; Reduced common-channel burden versus backward compatibility and specification scope.; Simple radio tests versus the geometry and processing required for network detection.
editorial.consequence: Keep the field small and evaluate it in the intended configured format.; Compare complete architectures and keep protocol compatibility separate from power and cost evidence.; Establish the evaluation relationship before treating prediction as a replacement for measurement.; Clarify shared-cell counting before assuming all candidate combinations fit.; Obtain plenary guidance and settle activation-window mapping.; Calibrate the abstraction against object-level performance under the same scenario.
editorial.novelty: Restores meeting-wide analysis across independent areas, distinguishing company positions from recorded replies and linking algorithm, protocol and radio constraints.
editorial.uncertainty: RAN4 company implementation and feasibility papers are not presented as adopted Calgary conclusions.; Detailed tables are absent in several extracted replies; no missing CSI-compression agreements or numerical distortion results are reconstructed.; The outgoing eight-SSB letter requests plenary direction and is not a plenary approval.; Waveform, channel coding, complete energy-saving down-selection and other Release-20 work remain outside this report rather than inferred from incomplete summaries.
editorial.analysis_excerpt: The two threads need to meet in an aligned evaluation. Passing a radio leakage or switching test does not prove that the selected set of observations produces acceptable detections. Conversely, a network result using helpful additional nodes does not automatically establish that each radio can meet its assumed input conditions. A scenario-specific test should keep the node geometry, detector settings and hardware assumptions visible from the RF measurement through the object decision.

topics.heading: Service differentiation enters an already constrained control channel
topics.finding: An additional service indication is feasible, with a constrained scope.
topics.mechanism: An uplink grant can influence which logical channels are served through logical-channel prioritization.
topics.tradeoff: Useful service differentiation versus control-message size and common access burden.
topics.next_step: Keep the field small and evaluate it in the intended configured format.
topics.analysis_excerpt: The next useful evidence is a concrete field design in its actual control format: what behavior it selects, how configuration governs its presence, and what size or decoding cost it introduces. RAN1's reply answers whether the direction is possible. The balance between useful differentiation and control overhead still depends on the detailed design.

topics.heading: Digital beamforming clears a protocol question rather than a cost test
topics.finding: RAN1 leaves device beamforming architecture to implementation; RAN4 cost arguments remain conditional.
topics.mechanism: Digital and analog spatial filtering move conversion and distribution costs between blocks.
topics.tradeoff: More digital chains versus removal of analog distribution and beamforming components.
topics.next_step: Compare complete architectures and keep protocol compatibility separate from power and cost evidence.
topics.analysis_excerpt: The implementation freedom preserved by RAN1 makes that comparison more important. If several architectures fit the same procedures, the standard need not pick a winner through an unsupported universal cost claim. RAN4 can describe which receiver behavior a test assumes and which architecture assumptions underpin a result. A protocol-compatible implementation and an economically preferable implementation are separate conclusions.

topics.heading: Learned prediction still lacks an agreed cross-site channel basis
topics.finding: RAN1 does not recommend the three proposed model shortcuts for non-collocated prediction.
topics.mechanism: Cross-site prediction depends on channel correlation that simple visibility labels do not supply.
topics.tradeoff: Reproducible evaluation versus realistic deployment variation and model complexity.
topics.next_step: Establish the evaluation relationship before treating prediction as a replacement for measurement.
topics.analysis_excerpt: Apple's earlier interoperability proposal identifies compatibility parameters such as pairing identity, ports, subbands and payload size. That helps define what an encoder and decoder must agree on, but it does not resolve either the channel-model relationship for prediction or the waveform assumptions for a learned feedback signal. The Calgary work is separating these contracts; an accuracy number cannot stand in for all of them.

topics.heading: Mobility capability reuse now has an explicit counting problem
topics.finding: RAN1 confirms capability reuse but requests clarification for a secondary cell shared by configurations.
topics.mechanism: Per-cell limits apply individually while across-cell resources cover the total candidate set.
topics.tradeoff: Reuse of existing capabilities versus correct accounting across multiple configurations.
topics.next_step: Clarify shared-cell counting before assuming all candidate combinations fit.
topics.analysis_excerpt: The work-item objective remains activation of secondary cells as part of the special-cell switch, with reuse of candidate measurement procedures where possible. The new reply advances capability alignment, but does not supply a measured interruption gain or settle every activation timing requirement. For implementers, progress is the narrower ability to apply known capability fields under explicit per-cell and shared limits, while tracking the unresolved shared-secondary-cell case.

topics.heading: More satellite synchronization beams need matching access windows
topics.finding: The eight-block extension is referred to plenary with access mapping and compatibility issues.
topics.mechanism: Synchronization visibility and usable random-access occasions must follow beam activation.
topics.tradeoff: Reduced common-channel burden versus backward compatibility and specification scope.
topics.next_step: Obtain plenary guidance and settle activation-window mapping.
topics.analysis_excerpt: This is related to, but distinct from, the 6G compensation work described before Calgary. Apple's satellite proposal allocates feeder-link Doppler compensation to the network and makes assumptions about how the device obtains timing and satellite information. The Release-20 beam-hopping extension adds a scheduling window for when access is usable. Neither an available synchronization beam nor a corrected frequency alone establishes that an access opportunity is valid at the needed time.

topics.heading: Sensing moves from a universal margin toward declared scenarios
topics.finding: RAN1 rejects a general single-node-to-network mapping while RAN4 tests remain implementation dependent.
topics.mechanism: Multiple views, detector processing and self-interference shape the result beyond echo signal quality.
topics.tradeoff: Simple radio tests versus the geometry and processing required for network detection.
topics.next_step: Calibrate the abstraction against object-level performance under the same scenario.

claims.claim: The Calgary record contains progress on several fronts, with different kinds of closure. Radio Access Network Working Group 1 (RAN1) accepts the feasibility of a service indication in uplink scheduling and confirms reuse of existing mobility capabilities. It finds no physical-layer change specific to a digital-beamforming device architecture. Yet its answers on learned measurement prediction and network sensing leave substantial evaluation work unresolved. Those distinctions matter to Radio Access Network Working Group 4 (RAN4), where company papers translate the proposed functions into hardware, measurement and testing choices.

claims.claim: Murata supplies a more general caution. Digital beamforming adds converters, mixers and digital processing paths, but can remove analog beamformers and radio-frequency distribution losses. It argues that converter resolution, integration, oscillator architecture and the location of spatial filtering all change the balance. BeammWave proposes recording a favorable silicon-area comparison for its evaluated implementations; Murata says an architecture-level block count cannot establish that either analog or digital is generally cheaper.
claims.passage: Compared with ABF, DBF requires more ADCs, DACs, mixers and associated signal paths. On the other hand, DBF does not require analog RF signal distribution or analog beamformers. It can therefore remove some RF components and reduce the insertion loss that may require additional amplifier stages in ABF. The cost impact should be considered based on the overall architecture, rather than only on the number of RF chains or data converters.

claims.claim: RAN4's non-collocated prediction study seeks to infer a target cell's layer-three received power from measurements at a different site and frequency. Nokia warns that the model could learn the particular cross-site realization used in training and fail to generalize. Its proposal was to await RAN1's channel-model guidance rather than assume that a familiar model already supplied the required relationship.
claims.passage: In AI-RRM Sub-case 2, the AI/ML model is trained to predict L3 cell-level measurements of non-collocated cell(s) on a target frequency layer, which are not on the same site as measured cell(s). The cross-site correlation learned by the model is determined by the channel model realization used for training, e.g., cross-site correlation. If the model is insufficiently generalized, it may perform well only for the realization it was trained on and degrade under different realizations, deployments, or UE speeds. This may lead to frequent model switching or fallback to legacy measurements, thereby losing the expected gains. Therefore, RAN4 should consider generalization aspects when selecting channel model for AI RRM Sub-case 2.

claims.claim: Ericsson's RAN4 feasibility paper discusses a different part of the chain. Full-duplex sensing must control leakage from its own transmitter; pulsed sensing introduces a blind zone determined by the pulse and switching behavior. The paper argues that another sensing mode or another node can cover a local blind zone, so one fixed switching-time limit would not represent all implementations. It proposes leaving synchronization choices open where relative over-the-air references can meet the task.
